key_insight: LIBERO-PeRM introduces a controlled benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation, separating whether a robot completes a task from whether it satisfies a user's preferences. This makes it possible to measure true personalization in embodied agents rather than just task success.
problem_solved: Existing robotic manipulation benchmarks mostly test generic task completion and do not cleanly evaluate preference satisfaction. The paper addresses the lack of a standardized benchmark for studying personalized robotic manipulation in household settings.
method: Introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark designed to evaluate preference learning in embodied robotic agents.
Structure evaluation around key research questions about how policies follow preferences, including zero-shot preference compliance.
Provide a controlled setup that distinguishes task execution quality from user-preference satisfaction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a clearer way to measure progress in personalization for robots, which is crucial for real-world home deployment. It can improve the development and comparison of policies that are not only effective, but also aligned with individual user needs.
